title: Work: Tackling Monotonous Tasks and Sharing the Load

words.exam_focus_zh: 阅读里常见 address the issue / address a problem 表示“处理问题”，是 tackle、deal with 的同义替换；听力填空注意拼写是双 d、双 s。

senses.definition_zh: 着手处理，解决（问题、需求）
senses.definition_en: to deal with a problem or a need
to speak formally to a group of people
the details of where someone lives; a formal speech

synonyms.nuance_zh: 比 address 更口语、更有“正面迎上去解决”的意味，常与 problem、issue、challenge 搭配。
synonyms.collocation: tackle a problem head-on（正面解决问题）

synonyms.nuance_zh: 强调问题最终被彻底解决、有了结果；address 只强调着手处理，不保证解决。

examples.sentence: The report recommends that local councils address the shortage of affordable housing before the situation worsens.
examples.translation_zh: 该报告建议地方议会在情况恶化之前解决经济适用房短缺的问题。
examples.note_zh: address + 负面名词（shortage、problem）是阅读和写作的高频组合。

examples.sentence: The mayor will address the conference on the second day, focusing on transport policy.
examples.translation_zh: 市长将在第二天的大会上致辞，重点谈交通政策。
examples.note_zh: 此处 address 是“向……讲话”，不要理解成“地址”。

words.exam_focus_zh: 写作 Task 2 讨论政策、动机时的核心名词，常与 financial、tax、offer 搭配；阅读中与 motivation、reward 互为同义替换。

senses.definition_zh: 激励措施，奖励（促使人行动的外部因素）
senses.definition_en: something that encourages a person to do something

synonyms.nuance_zh: 多指内在的心理驱动力；incentive 多指外部给出的奖励或优惠条件。
指实际给出的回报本身；incentive 强调它起到的“促使人行动”的作用。

examples.sentence: Tax incentives have been introduced to encourage companies to invest in cleaner technology.
examples.translation_zh: 政府出台了税收优惠政策，鼓励企业投资更清洁的技术。
examples.note_zh: 写作中谈政府措施时，introduce / offer incentives 是很实用的搭配。

examples.sentence: For many employees, the main incentive to stay is not salary but a sense of being valued.
examples.translation_zh: 对许多员工来说，留下来的主要动因不是薪水，而是被重视的感觉。
examples.note_zh: the incentive to do sth 是常见结构，注意用不定式。

words.exam_focus_zh: 动词“委派”与名词“代表”同形但读音不同（名词读 /ˈdelɪɡət/），听力中常靠词尾元音辨别；写作谈管理时 delegate tasks 是常用搭配。

senses.definition_zh: 把（任务、权力）交给下属，委派
senses.definition_en: to give part of your work or authority to someone else
a person chosen to attend a meeting or speak for a group

synonyms.nuance_zh: 只强调把任务分给某人，不一定交出权力；delegate 还含“授权、放手让别人做”的意思。
synonyms.collocation: assign tasks to team members（给团队成员分派任务）

synonyms.nuance_zh: 更正式，强调基于信任把重要的事交给别人。
synonyms.collocation: entrust somebody with something（把某事托付给某人）

examples.sentence: Effective managers know when to delegate routine tasks so that they can concentrate on strategic decisions.
examples.translation_zh: 高效的管理者知道何时把常规任务分派出去，以便专注于战略性决策。
examples.note_zh: delegate 后直接接任务，不接人；要接人需用 delegate sth to sb。

examples.sentence: Each delegate at the summit received a summary of the proposals in advance.
examples.translation_zh: 峰会的每位代表都提前收到了一份提案摘要。
examples.note_zh: 这里 delegate 是名词“代表”，读 /ˈdelɪɡət/。

words.exam_focus_zh: 常用于描述工作性质或声音，阅读、听力中与 repetitive、tedious 互为同义替换；拼写注意 mono- + ton-，中间不是 -tonn-。

senses.definition_en: (of a sound) never changing in tone

synonyms.nuance_zh: 强调反复做同一个动作，中性偏贬；monotonous 更强调“毫无变化、令人厌倦”。
强调耗时又让人厌倦，多形容过程、讲话或文字，不常形容声音。
synonyms.collocation: a tedious lecture（冗长乏味的讲座）

examples.sentence: Although the factory work was monotonous, the steady income allowed him to support his family.
examples.translation_zh: 虽然工厂的工作很单调，但稳定的收入让他能养家。
examples.note_zh: 让步状语从句 Although… 是写作中对比利弊的常用结构。

examples.sentence: Researchers found that monotonous tasks reduce attention spans and increase error rates.
examples.translation_zh: 研究者发现，单调的任务会缩短注意力持续时间并提高出错率。
examples.note_zh: reduce / increase 搭配注意力和出错率，适合 Task 2 论证。

words.exam_focus_zh: 阅读中常替换 carry out、conduct，后接 research、study、survey、review 等；写作中比 do 更正式，也用于 undertake to do 表示“承诺”。

senses.definition_en: to start and carry out a task or piece of work
to promise that you will do something

synonyms.nuance_zh: 强调把计划落实到完成，常接 research、survey、experiment。
synonyms.collocation: carry out a survey（开展调查）

synonyms.nuance_zh: 更口语，强调接手额外的工作或责任。
synonyms.collocation: take on extra responsibilities（承担额外责任）

examples.sentence: The university undertook a three-year study into the effects of remote working on productivity.
examples.translation_zh: 这所大学开展了一项为期三年的研究，考察远程办公对生产率的影响。
examples.note_zh: undertake + study / research 是阅读中常见的正式表达。

examples.sentence: The government has undertaken to review the policy within two years.
examples.translation_zh: 政府已承诺在两年内重新审视该政策。
examples.note_zh: undertake to do sth 意为“承诺做某事”，不要误读成“着手做”。

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Hey Daniel, how's the new job going? I heard you're managing a small team now.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: It's good, but honestly the paperwork is pretty monotonous. I spend half my morning copying figures into spreadsheets.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That sounds like something you could delegate. Isn't there a junior colleague who could take it on?

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: There is, but I feel a bit guilty handing over the boring bits.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: I get that, but if you never delegate routine tasks, you'll never get to the strategic work — and the company clearly has an incentive for you to do that.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: True. My manager said the same thing. She wants me to address the backlog in our client reports first.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: That's a sensible place to start. Once that's sorted, you could undertake a proper review of the whole process.

dialogue.speaker: Daniel
dialogue.text: I might, yes. I just need to be careful not to overload the new starter. I'll begin with a couple of tasks a week and check in with her regularly.

quiz.question: In the sentence "The committee was set up to address the growing problem of youth unemployment", "address" is closest in meaning to:
quiz.explanation_zh: 此处 address 后接 problem，意为“着手处理、解决”，与 tackle 同义。speak formally to 是另一个义项，但需要接人（address the audience）。

quiz.question: Which sentence uses "delegate" correctly as a noun meaning “代表”?
options: She delegate the report to her assistant yesterday.
Each delegate was given a name badge at the conference.
The manager delegate authority to the team regularly.
He is very delegate when handling complaints.
quiz.explanation_zh: B 中 delegate 作名词，指参会“代表”，读音为 /ˈdelɪɡət/。A、C 把动词当成了原形直接接宾语，时态和形式都不对；D 把名词当形容词用，错误。
